chunks: And that which was narrated - Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Muhrim (one in Ihram), if he catches a pigeon, then upon him is a sheep; and if he kills its chicks, then upon him is a camel; and if he treads on the eggs, then upon him is a Dirham. This is not contradictory to what we have presented earlier, because the first report is interpreted as referring to one who slaughtered the pigeon while he was Muhtal (not in Ihram), and the second is interpreted as referring to one who slaughtered it while he was Muhrim (in Ihram), and there is no contradiction between them.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: One not in Ihram (in a state of permissibility)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a pilgrim in Ihram who kills a pigeon?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between reports by distinguishing the state of the pilgrim: the first report applies to one who was already Ihram-free, while the second applies to one currently in the state of Ihram, thereby establishing specific compensation (kaffarah) for pigeons, chicks, and eggs. This distinction highlights the precision of Shia jurists in reconciling hadith narratives by contextualizing the temporal status of the pilgrim. The ruling underscores the legal principle that violations during the sacred state carry distinct financial penalties compared to those outside it.
